clue.text: Boat found on bar

definitions.meaning: a two-masted sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rig
a large drinking glass for sherry or beer, as seen on a pub counter

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sailing ship with several masts and a tall glass served across a pub counter.

clue.text: Looking up archbishop's clothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: EBOR is the signature of the Archbishop of York, from the Latin name for York

explanation.surface: Someone peering upwards at a senior churchman's vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: EBOR, the Archbishop of York's signature, read upwards gives the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown or vestment is a piece of clothing, here singular as the clue's mass noun allows.

clue.text: Eventually getting maps over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another means the first sits above the second in the grid

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: Someone finally obtaining road maps after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean finally, after a long delay, so the phrase swaps directly for the adverb.

clue.text: Famous tipster hit the road

parts.note: a famous person is a star
a tout sells racing tips

explanation.surface: A well-known racing tipster setting off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR is a noun for a famous person, used here as the clue's adjective is read loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the road is an idiom for setting off on a journey, the same as to depart.

clue.text: Old Greek dares somehow to collect toll

indicators.note: to collect means the scrambled letters gather the other piece inside them
somehow says the letters are put together in some unspecified new way

parts.note: to toll a bell is to chime it

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek daring, by some means, to gather a tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' scrambles the given word, and 'to collect' has it gather the bell sound into its middle. 'Toll' looks like a tax or charge but is what a bell does.
explanation.definitionFit: The Syracusan mathematician of the third century BC is a famous ancient Greek.

clue.text: Covet a bizarre bird

indicators.note: bizarre means strange or twisted, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Coveting an odd bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird with an upturned bill, one particular species of bird.

clue.text: A clever rhyme or subtle teaser I constitute

definitions.text: A clever rhyme or subtle teaser I constitute

parts.words: A clever rhyme or subtle teaser I constitute
parts.note: the clue speaks as itself: take the opening letter of each of its eight words and they spell out what it is

explanation.surface: A riddle boasting of its own cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: No indicator word is spare: every word of the clue gives its initial, and those initials name the kind of puzzle the clue is.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse or puzzle whose initial letters spell a word is exactly what the clue's own initials do.

clue.text: Boat for Charlie to deliver

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to utter a speech is to deliver it

explanation.surface: A vessel intended for a man called Charlie to hand over.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fast vessel, such as a coastguard ship, is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Boom concealed in the Forth River

indicators.note: concealed in says the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A boom hidden away in Scotland's River Forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed in' points to the letters spanning the end of Forth and the start of River. The Forth is a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: To boom is to flourish or prosper, as an economy does, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Dance with earl in anticipation

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Dancing with a nobleman in eager expectation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is the expectation of something wished for, close to anticipation.

clue.text: Wine following pudding gives one the shakes later

indicators.note: following means the first-named piece comes after the other one

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Wine after dessert leaves a diner trembling later on.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for the dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: A later tremor following a main earthquake is a set of further shakes.

clue.text: Order tinned stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook in a jumble, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Ordering canned stew.
explanation.definitionFit: An indent is an official requisition or order for goods, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Dispatch old penny publication

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an edition is one publication of a book or paper

explanation.surface: Send off an old penny-dreadful issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispatch as a noun means speed or promptness, which an expedition also means in older use.

clue.text: Evil and hatred consuming other ranks

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing the other piece inside

parts.note: enmity is hostility or hatred
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, enlisted soldiers

explanation.surface: Wickedness and loathing devouring the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: The word's core sense is great wickedness, a grave evil or outrage.

clue.text: Soldier's gone for a meal

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier
past means gone by

explanation.surface: A soldier who has left to get some food.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.

clue.text: Joiner wears tie on the golf course

indicators.note: the tie has the joining word put on inside it, as wearing means having something on

parts.note: a strap ties things together
the conjunction and joins words

explanation.surface: A carpenter putting on a necktie before a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter but is the conjunction AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunker of sand is a hazard found on a golf course.

clue.text: Goes on about tax officer arguing

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: to add is to go on saying more
TO is short for tax officer

explanation.surface: Someone ranting about a tax inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in disagreement is the idiom's meaning, matching arguing.

clue.text: Scottish leaders retaliate and clean up the streets

parts.note: the leading pair of letters of Scottish
to avenge is to take revenge, retaliate

explanation.surface: Scottish leaders hit back and tidy the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge originally meant to clean streets of refuse, a scavenger being a street cleaner.

clue.text: Little girl interrupts salesmen going up for a rest

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reads the letters backwards
interrupts means breaking into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
Di is a short form of Diana

explanation.surface: A small girl barges in on salesmen climbing upstairs for a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' puts the girl inside the salesmen first, then 'going up' turns that whole run, not just the salesmen. A spider is a long-legged cue rest in snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, a spider is a raised rest for the cue, used over other balls.

clue.text: Complaints drop off in bad weather

parts.note: colds are minor ailments, complaints
to nap is to drop off to sleep

explanation.surface: Moaning stops when nodding off in foul weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spell of freezing temperatures is a kind of bad weather.

clue.text: Dagger found on page showing blouse undone

indicators.note: undone means unfastened or ruined, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A knife discovered on a page revealing an unbuttoned blouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The printer's dagger mark, used for footnotes, is a symbol seen on a printed page.

clue.text: Note girl put back in prayer book

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: put back means the word is reversed

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl's note slipped back into a prayer book.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is a book of prayers and texts for the Mass.

clue.text: An accident ruined his map

indicators.note: ruined means spoiled, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's map ruined in an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is a minor accident or misfortune.

clue.text: Skip ill-used religious sayings

parts.note: to skip off is to beat it, run away

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters that follow are treated badly and jumbled

explanation.surface: Skipping over misused holy sayings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' rearranges USED into UDES. Read 'ill-used' not as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The blessings beginning the Sermon on the Mount are a set of religious sayings.

clue.text: Lean part of the anatomy

definitions.meaning: to lean over to one side, as a ship does
the back part of the foot

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels tilts sideways, and the same word is the rear of the human foot.

clue.text: Old king detailed brave soldier

indicators.note: detailed means having its tail, the last letter, removed

parts.note: Herod was the king of Judea in the Gospels

explanation.surface: An ancient king described as a courageous fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a person of great bravery, such as a valiant soldier.

clue.text: A visual display of yellow in the atmosphere

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: an aura is a surrounding atmosphere
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A yellow light show in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern or southern lights are a natural visual display in the sky.

clue.text: A Yank tucking into eggs is dangerous when driving

indicators.note: tucking into means being placed inside the other piece

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
to drag is to pull, yank

explanation.surface: An American eating eggs at the wheel is a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is a pull. The definition is a description of the anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry aggressive behaviour by motorists is a menace on the roads, described by what it is.
